reply_text:
I checked claude-4's buffer for the original asks. Here's what I found.㊥ (`"marked up correctly in an earlier claude round"`) I checked claude-4's buffer, and neither ask was ever marked 🈸. Stop C was first asked in the middle of a ㊥ gist, in an auto-bellback turn ("Shall I authorize stop C as the first fix, or would you rather review the findings first?"). The push first appeared as a 🈝 promise, repeated four times: "If all 20 rows match, I'll come back to you before pushing". When the rows did match, the first actual ask was already a 🈳, combined with the stop C reminder. After that the 🈳 was repeated eleven times in slightly different words, and your "yes" answered the last one.

㊣ (`"still waiting is a reminder about an earlier ask"`) I agree that's what 🈳 means here. A reminder should link to the ask it repeats, and the agreement belongs to that original ask. Here, though, there was no marked ask for the reminders to point back to. So the recorder had nothing to agree to, and 象 had nothing to keep open across those eleven repeats.

🈖 (what that shows) Most of the failure is at the point where the ask is made. claude-4 kept the promise ("I'll ask you before pushing") in substance: it did ask before pushing. But the moment a promise turns into a question is the one moment that needs a 🈸, and it came out as 🈳. Stop C went the same way: the question sat inside a gist, then went straight to 🈳.

㭭 (two changes)
1. **Proforma line (CLAUDE.md).** The first time you ask Joe for a decision, use 🈸, one question per paragraph. Use 🈳 only to remind him of a question already asked, and quote that question in the bracket. That reminder rule is the same quoted-bracket link I built yesterday for replies.
2. **Recorder.** A 🈳 whose bracket quotes an earlier 🈸 counts as a reminder of that offer, so "yes" agrees to the original. A 🈳 with nothing to link to, like claude-4's, counts as an offer in its own right, one option per question. A bare "yes" to several questions accepts all of them, which is how you meant it and how claude-4 acted.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I make both changes?

The recorder only counts 🈸 paragraphs as offers. claude-4 understood you correctly anyway: it pushed `8c5a3146` to Rob's main and sent the stop C fix to codex-24. So nothing went wrong in the work. The gap is that the agreement ledger shows nothing for that turn, so neither the push nor the go-ahead for stop C is recorded as agreed.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(why it's a good exercise) The one paragraph shows four gaps:
1. **The mark.** claude-4 marked a request for permission as 🈳. That reads naturally, but `reply-offer-record` (`agreement_record.clj:73`) only reads 🈸, so there was no offer to agree to.
2. **Two questions in one paragraph.** "May I push `8c5a3146`? And should stop C be the first fix?" You meant yes to both, and claude-4 acted on both. With them as two 🈸 paragraphs, a bare "yes" would have come back as ambiguous instead. This is the "and between two nouns" problem again, at the level of a question.
3. **Where the question was asked.** claude-4 asked it twice: once in its REPL reply, then again in an auto-bellback turn after codex-27 hit its capacity limit. Your "yes" answered the second one, which came from a bell. Bells aren't in 象's ledger yet, so even with the right mark, the port it opened would be in the wrong place. That's step 1 of the order of work I just added to E-agency-work-orders.
4. **The push is a commit nobody captured.** Even with the agreement recorded, nothing links "Rob's main is at `8c5a3146`" to it, so the obligation would show as still owed. That's the same gap as claude-7's /tmp commit.

previous_reply_acts.text: (a fix for 1 and 2, small) Treat a 🈳 paragraph made only of questions as an offer, with one option per question. Read a bare "yes" to a multi-question offer as accepting all of them, not as ambiguous: that is what you meant, and what claude-4 did. "yes 1" would still pick one. The alternative is to leave the code alone and add a line to the proforma: "permission requests are 🈸, one question per paragraph". I'd do both, because agents will keep reaching for 🈳.
